first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing (memory_73) the salient reflex, but the stated objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and a discount war against a lower-priced entrant tends to buy acquisition at the cost of margin and account quality — memory_73's summary reports acquisition and revenue lift but says nothing about retention, discount-cohort LTV, or whether the lift persisted past the promo window. The two internal declines (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are the deteriorating fundamentals and are the more durable place to spend the single slot. Onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing completion plausibly relieves both, which is why I intend simplify_onboarding over activation_messaging (memory_91) for this slot. Two caveats drive the verification picks and the guarded scale. First, memory_31 (cut signup fields) and memory_86 (shorten onboarding) may well be consolidated restatements of the same underlying experiment; if so my evidence base is one study, not two, and the apparent convergence is an artifact of summarization. Second, both memories are recorded against proxy outcomes — activation, completion, time-to-value — not qualified revenue. Friction removed at signup is friction that reappears downstream: fewer required fields can mean thinner qualification data, worse routing, and lower-quality accounts that activate and then churn, which would show up as a win on the measured metric while eroding the actual objective. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) points the other way and is a reason not to strip qualification from paths that feed pipeline. So: pull the source records for memory_86 and memory_31 to test independence and to see which outcomes were actually measured. If they prove to be one experiment, or if neither tracked revenue quality, I keep this a small guarded test — self-serve SMB segment only, enterprise/demo path untouched, with lead-quality, downstream-conversion, and retention guardrails instrumented alongside completion rate. If they are independent and did track quality, scaling up next cycle is justified.
